data.name: Photine
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Phōtīnē means 'bright, shining one'. In Christianity, it refers to Saint Photina, also known as Veronica, who is believed to have wiped the face of Jesus as He carried the Cross.

in_hebrew.name: פוטינה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פוטינה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו 'מוארת' או 'נושאת אור'. השם קשור למושג האור הרוחני והאור של אלוהים בכתבי הקודש. השם פוטינה משמש כזכרון לאור האלוהי המלווה את המאמינים בדרכם הרוחנית.

in_greek.name: Φωτίνη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Φωτίνη προέρχεται από το ελληνικό φωτός και σημαίνει 'αυτή που φέρνει φως' ή 'φωτεινή'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το φως συμβολίζει την πνευματική φώτιση και τη σοφία που προέρχεται από τον Θεό. Το όνομα Φωτίνη αντικατοπτρίζει την πνευματική σημασία του φωτός στην παράδοση των πρώτων Χριστιανών.

in_latin.name: Photine
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Photine originem habet in lingua Graeca et significat 'illa quae lucem affert' seu 'splendida'. In Ecclesia primitiva, lux erat symbolum sapientiae et illuminationis spiritualis. Nomen Photine itaque refert connotationem spiritualem et mysticam, quae Christianis fidelibus comitatur in via salutis.

in_english.name: Photine
in_english.long_meaning: The name Photine originates from the Greek word for 'light' (φως, phos) and signifies 'one who brings light' or 'radiant'. This etymology links Photine to biblical themes where light represents spiritual illumination, wisdom, and divine presence. Historically, the name Photine has been associated with the virtues of enlightenment and guidance in the Christian tradition. It symbolizes the bearer as a source of inspiration and spiritual light.

saint_reference.note: Saint Photine is recognized in some Christian traditions as a saint and is associated with early Christian martyrdom.

data.cultural_impact: Saint Photina or Veronica is revered in Christian tradition as the woman who embraced faith upon meeting Jesus. Their encounter is depicted in various artworks, and the story has been a source of inspiration for countless hymns, sculptures, paintings, and literature throughout history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Photine," derived from the Greek word "phōtīnē," emphasizes the radiance and light emanating from the divine presence of Jesus Christ. It is a constant reminder of the transformative power of faith, which illuminates the lives of believers. In the story of Saint Photina, we also witness the spiritual journey of an individual, who chose to seek the truth and convert to the faith. This inspires us to follow the example of Saint Photina and her profound commitment to the teachings of Jesus Christ.

historical_references.reference: In the Acts of Philip, a deacon in the early Christian church, Photine is mentioned as a woman who was converted by Philip and baptized. She later relapsed into sin, but was eventually restored to the church through the intercession of the apostle Peter.
historical_references.time_period: Early Christian period, likely late 1st or early 2nd century

historical_references.reference: Photine is also mentioned in the Acts of Thecla, another early Christian text. In this version, Photine is a friend of Thecla, who becomes a follower of Paul and is passionate in her faith. Photine, however, is depicted as a skeptic and a temptress, and her interactions with Thecla contribute to the development of Thecla's own deep commitment to Christianity.
historical_references.time_period: Early Christian period, likely late 2nd or early 3rd century

name_in_real_life.story: Grace Photine, a minister in Dublin, Ireland, shares that their name Photine meaning "Bright, shining one" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Photine, derived from the Greek word for light, symbolizes the inner spiritual illumination and enlightenment in a Christian's life journey. It is a reminder to embrace the light of God and let it illuminate one's path towards righteousness and holiness.
